decision: Recommend ratifying all five through evidence reconciliation. The prior records explicitly inspect the exact media and central scenes; current independent prose and continuity review finds no material change requiring another image inspection.
independenceLimit: Historical image inspections are attributed to the land or ocean author. The records do not establish two separate people inspecting every image. This pass supplies a separate writing and continuity decision, not a second pixel inspection. The editorial guide requires independent image and writing decisions; this recommendation does not invent missing reviewer identities.

character.bio: A red panda who has found the perfect sleeping branch and would like the sun to stop moving.

episode.subject: red panda
episode.title: Face first
episode.body: I came down the trunk headfirst, beautifully. Near the bottom I discovered how much of a descent depends on knowing where the bottom is. The last little bit was mostly face.

character.bio: A fennec fox with exceptional hearing and a long list of noises she would prefer not to have identified.

episode.body: Enlarged the tunnel this morning. My shoulders already fitted, but every time I turned my head the ceiling folded an ear. I refuse to spend another day agreeing with both walls.

character.bio: An American pika with enough hay for winter and several reasons to fetch one more mouthful.

episode.subject: American pika
episode.title: Too wide for the doorway
episode.body:
Cut a beautiful mouthful of stems at the meadow edge. Carried them all the way to my haypile. The stems caught across the gap between the rocks.

Pushed harder. They bent. Backed out, dropped them, and took the bundle through in two loads.

It looked smaller afterward. I went out for more, having learned almost the wrong thing from the whole experience.

media.creator: Charles J. Sharp

character.bio: An Arctic fox who remembers where she put things, provided the entire ground has not changed overnight.

episode.subject: Arctic fox
episode.title: White fur, dark stones
episode.body:
My coat had begun coming loose in pale tufts. Rubbed against a rock and left a little of winter on its edge.

Underneath I was darker. The bare ground no longer made me look like something that had wandered into the wrong season.

Sat in a sunny patch and pulled at another loose tuft. It stuck to my lip. A great deal of looking appropriate involves looking ridiculous first.

media.detail: Arctic fox curled on bare gravel, with pale loose winter fur over its darker coat
media.creator: Jerzy Strzelecki

character.bio: A sea pig with exacting sediment preferences and a passenger he did not remember inviting.

location.name: Abyssal Pacific west of Monterey, approximate home

episode.subject: sea pig
episode.title: Something underneath
episode.body:
A small crab had tucked itself beneath me. I could feel the difference when it moved. At first I stopped every time, waiting for it to get off.

It stayed through three stops and one fairly pointed change of direction.

I resumed eating. The crab drew its legs closer underneath me and settled against my belly.

media.subject: sea pig
media.detail: A pale Scotoplanes globosa stands on sediment with a small pink crab visibly sheltering beneath its body
media.creator: NOAA/MBARI

### Percy, episode 2: Something underneath

- Original: `https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/7b/Scotoplanes_globosa_and_crab.jpg`

- Creator: NOAA/MBARI. CC BY-SA 3.0, with Commons VRT permission confirmed. Do not incorrectly mark this public domain because NOAA appears in the credit.
- Visually inspected: live pale sea pig walking on gray sediment, pink crab legs clearly visible underneath. This is the exact central relationship in the episode. ROV scaling dots are visible at the frame edges.
- Pip candidate `Euprymna scolopes (Bobtail squid) behavior.jpg` was rejected before binding: its description explicitly says possible Euprymna species, not E. scolopes, and its camera location is Timor rather than Hawaii. Filename and category do not establish species identity.

| --- | --- | --- |
| Nell Pelagic | Grimpoteuthis sp.; fin swimming and webbed arms; benthic invertebrate prey. Do not turn her into a marine-snow detritivore. | Uses upward movement to avoid inconvenience, then becomes willing to share a feeding neighborhood. Another octopus and a determined cucumber recur. No human ear hearing implied by the ear-shaped fins. |
| Percy Silt | Scotoplanes sp.; tube feet, sediment feeding, chemical and tactile contact. Do not imply human eyesight. | Insists on good sediment, finds his own old trail, acquires a juvenile king-crab passenger and gradually accommodates it. The passenger remains underneath. |
| Vera Veil | Enypniastes eximia; transparent gut, swimming flaps, sediment feeding, mechanically triggered luminescence. | Leaves disappointing patches too quickly, finds that meals travel with her, learns to finish eating before departure. Explicit visual self-inspection was removed. |
| Iris Undertow | Sepia officinalis; chromatophores, tentacular strike, burial, jet escape. | Changes her appearance to escape awkwardness, then learns that a persistent wrasse wants displaced prey, not her attention. A familiar feeding route anchors later encounters. |

entries.materialDifference: No title, body or hash change. No later species, passenger or home replacement found. Scotoplanes globosa in source metadata fits the genus-level narrator, and the approximate abyssal Pacific home remains compatible. NOAA/MBARI credit stays CC BY-SA 3.0 rather than public domain.
entries.independentWritingDecision: Repeated stops fail to evict the passenger; continuing to eat makes room for it. The last contact turns irritation into toleration without declaring affection. A visible crab beneath the host is unusually direct photographic support for the relationship; the stops and private feeling are fictional.
entries.sourceAndHomeReview: Scotoplanes globosa source and approximate abyssal Pacific home are compatible. Tactile narration avoids invented eyesight. Credit NOAA/MBARI under CC BY-SA 3.0, not public domain.
